               RAAS: LLM Agentic System Architecture Search with GRPO

                           Jiayi Yang* Guancheng Wan* Man Zhang Mang Ye†
                              School of Computer Science, Wuhan University, China
                          {yangjiayi, guanchengwan, manzhang1, yemang}@whu.edu.cn
                                                    GitHub: github.com/ridlog/raas
                                           *
                                               Equal contribution. † Corresponding author.



                         Abstract
Large Language Model (LLM) agentic systems solve com-
plex tasks through coordinated workflows, but design-
ing them remains labor-intensive. The Agentic Supernet
paradigm automates this by optimizing a probabilistic ar-
chitecture space, yet suffers from critical evaluation insta-
bilities: absolute performance scores entangle architectural
merit with query difficulty, while single-execution proto-
cols capture execution randomness rather than true capa-
bility. These instabilities lead to unreliable search dynam-
ics where simple queries inflate weak designs and challeng-
ing queries suppress strong ones. We introduce RAAS (Ro-
bust Architecture Adaptive Search), which establishes more
stable and fair evaluation through two synergistic mecha-
nisms. Contextual Architecture Orchestration (CAO) dis-
entangles quality from task difficulty by evaluating cohorts
of candidate architectures on identical queries, deriving
context-aware merit signals through peer-group compari-
son. Multi-Trial Assessment Synthesis (MTAS) reduces
execution variance by aggregating performance across mul-
tiple independent trials, producing statistically robust capa-         Figure 1. An illustration of the core problem and our proposed
bility estimates. Together, these mechanisms provide more              solution. (A) Problem: Evaluation Instabilities. Easy queries
reliable signals for architecture discovery. Experiments               inflate weak architectures while hard queries depress strong ones
on six benchmarks spanning mathematical reasoning, code                (task-difficulty entanglement), and single-execution assessments
generation, and one multi-step tool-use benchmark show                 capture transient artifacts rather than true capability (execution
                                                                       variance). (B) RAAS: Stable Evaluation through Synergistic
that RAAS consistently improves over strong baselines, im-
                                                                       Design. RAAS evaluates cohorts of architectures on the same
proving HumanEval pass@1 from 92.23% to 96.31% and
                                                                       query through multiple independent trials. CAO derives contex-
MATH accuracy from 52.08% to 60.87%, while maintain-                   tual merit signals via peer comparison, while MTAS synthesizes
ing practical efficiency. These results suggest that robust            multi-trial outcomes for statistical robustness, together enabling
evaluation is a useful ingredient for agentic architecture             more reliable architecture discovery.
search in the studied settings.

Figure 5. Ablation study of RAAS components. We systematically analyze the contribution of CAO and MTAS modules by comparing:
(1) MaAS baseline, (2) MaAS with entropy regularization only, (3) RAAS with CAO only (no MTAS multi-trial synthesis), and (4) full
RAAS (CAO + MTAS). The results demonstrate that both contextual orchestration and multi-trial synthesis contribute synergistically to
performance gains, with their combination achieving the best results across all benchmarks.

                                                                     ❸ Favorable trade-off: Figure 6 places RAAS in a favorable
                                                                     cost-performance region among the evaluated single-agent
                                                                     and multi-agent systems.

                                                                     5. Conclusion
                                                                     Our work addresses evaluation instabilities in automated
                                                                     agentic architecture search, where absolute performance
                                                                     metrics conflate intrinsic architectural merit with extrinsic
                                                                     task-specific difficulty, and single-execution assessments
                                                                     capture stochastic artifacts rather than consistent capability.
                                                                     RAAS introduces a dual-stabilization framework through
Figure 6. Cost-performance trade-off analysis across different       two complementary mechanisms: Contextual Architecture
methods.                                                             Orchestration (CAO) performs cohort-based peer compar-
4.5. Effectiveness (Q4)                                              ison on identical queries to derive zero-centered, context-
                                                                     aware merit signals that factor out task difficulty, while
Figure 5 quantifies module contributions. Removing CAO
                                                                     Multi-Trial Assessment Synthesis (MTAS) aggregates mul-
drops performance near MaAS, confirming the need for
                                                                     tiple independent executions to produce statistically robust
contextual baselines. Disabling MTAS reintroduces execu-
                                                                     capability estimates that filter execution randomness. This
tion volatility and reduces final accuracy. Moderate cohort
                                                                     design provides more reliable signals for architecture dis-
sizes (N ∈ [4, 8]) balance signal quality and cost; K=3
                                                                     covery within the supernet paradigm. Empirically, RAAS
is often sufficient, with diminishing returns beyond K>5.
                                                                     yields substantial improvements on the evaluated math and
Full RAAS (CAO+MTAS) yields the best results across
                                                                     code benchmarks, and also improves performance on GAIA
benchmarks.
                                                                     as a multi-step tool-use benchmark: 60.87% on MATH,
                                                                     95.16% on GSM8K, 96.31% on HumanEval, 84.18% on
4.6. Cost Analysis (Q5)
                                                                     MBPP, and 20.84% on GAIA, achieving +5.41 average im-
Beyond accuracy, we compare performance-cost trade-offs              provement over the strongest baseline in our comparison
on MATH, as visualized in Figure 6.                                  while maintaining practical computational efficiency. We
   RAAS achieves 60.87% accuracy with $0.31 per query,               therefore view robust evaluation as a useful ingredient for
improving accuracy by 8.8 points over MaAS while reduc-              agentic architecture search in the studied settings, while
ing cost by 6%. The analysis reveals key efficiency insights         broader validation on more interactive multi-turn workflows
about computational resource allocation and architectural            remains an important direction for future work. Future re-
search strategies. Obs. ❶ Strong cost-effectiveness: RAAS            search directions include extending to richer multi-turn in-
delivers the best performance among the compared meth-               teractive scenarios, developing adaptive allocation strate-
ods with competitive computational cost. Obs. ❷ Efficient            gies for cohort size and trial count, establishing theoretical
design discovery: The system reduces costs through better            convergence guarantees for merit-weighted adaptation, and
architecture selection, avoiding redundant exploration and           investigating generalization across distribution shifts and
early convergence while maintaining search diversity. Obs.           novel task domains.
